newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Market makers drive Belgian bonds higher.
newsitem.headline: Market makers drive Belgian bonds higher.

text.p: Market makers pushed Belgian linear bonds (OLOs) higher in morning trading on Wednesday, reviving interest in the medium- to long-term maturities.
But traders said there was little "core" business, with end-investors still sidelined and all eyes on the flood of U.S. data due out on Thursday and Friday US-ECI.
"There is not that much real business. It is mostly market makers trying to get people interested," one trader said.
They said that in contrast with Tuesday when all the buying interest was in the short maturities, Wednesday saw a revival of interest in 10-year paper and longer.
"We are strong with Bunds this morning, although the spread has widened slightly," one trader said.
"People are buying Belgian paper against Bunds in the hope of making a profit on the spread when the market turns down again," he added.
The Belgian bond market tends to lag Germany more on the downturn than on the moves upward.

At 0900 GMT the benchmark 10-year OLO BE286= yielded 5.59 percent against 5.63 late on Tuesday, and the spread over Bunds MEUR was wavering at between 10 and 11 basis points compared with Tuesday's nine to 10 basis points.
Front-month futures were 31 basis points or 0.25 percent higher at 122.17, a similar percentage rise as seen on Bunds.

Traders said the immediate direction would depend largely on the U.S. figures -- particularly July non-farm payrolls and the National Association of Purchasing Managers index, and June personal income, spending and average hourly income figures.
Although there have been no signs so far of emerging inflationary pressure, nervous market players will be watching like hawks for any cloud on the horizon, traders said.
